desc:
A grid uses these codes: 0 empty cell, 1 wall, 2 your starting cell, 10 + i the key number i (lying on that cell), and 20 + i the door number i. If there are m keys, their numbers are exactly 0 .. m-1 (each key appears once), and each door number appears at most once and is smaller than m.

In one step you move up, down, left or right. You cannot enter a wall. Stepping onto a key cell picks the key up (keys are never used up). You may enter the cell of door i only if you already hold key i. Return the minimum number of steps after which you hold all m keys, or -1 if that is impossible.

grid = [[ 2,  0, 11],
        [ 1,  1, 21],
        [10,  0,  0]]

result = 6      (right, right: key 1; down through door 1, down, left, left: key 0)
constraints: Exactly one cell is 2; there are m keys, 1 ≤ m ≤ 6, with codes 10 .. 10+m-1 each appearing exactly once
Door codes 20 + i appear at most once each, with i < m
hints: The same cell visited with different sets of keys behaves differently. What should the BFS state contain?
State = (row, col, set of keys held), with the key set stored as a bitmask. At most 6 keys means at most 64 masks.

From a state try the four neighbours: skip walls and doors whose key bit is missing; if the neighbour is a key cell, set its bit. The first time the mask has all m bits set, the current layer number is the answer.
editorial: Because a door can only be passed with the right key, being on a cell is not enough information: the keys in hand decide where you can go next. So the node is (r, c, mask) with mask a bitmask of the keys held. There are at most rows × cols × 2m = 30 × 30 × 64 = 57,600 such nodes.

All moves cost one step, so BFS over these nodes finds the minimum. From (r, c, mask) look at each neighbour: ignore walls; ignore a door i if bit i is not in the mask; if the neighbour holds key i, the new mask is mask | (1 << i). Mark states visited when they are pushed. The search stops when the mask equals (1 << m) - 1.

Keys never disappear, so masks only grow, and each state is expanded once: O(rows × cols × 2<sup>m</sup>) time and memory. If the queue empties first, some key sits behind a door that can never be opened, and the answer is -1.
